findings.title: All-groups VIEW permission is treated as manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() treats a grant of either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource as success. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE, and V1 canManage() only checks the manage-users role, so this is not the intended scope model. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls requireManage() before creating a group and applying its attributes, so an admin who was given only Groups VIEW can create top-level groups. The new GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() javadoc repeats the mistake (it says V2 manage is true for VIEW or MANAGE), and GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest never asserts that VIEW alone cannot create or update groups.

findings.title: Member search filter uses authz resource IDs, not group IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission() and adds that same value to the returned set. hasPermission() looks the id up with resourceStore.findByName(), but per-group resources are stored with the realm group id as the name (resolveGroup returns group.getId()) and a different authorization-resource UUID as getId(). The lookup misses, falls back to the all-groups resource, and never evaluates that group's own policies. The IDs handed to UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource via session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, and to getUsersCount(), are therefore not group ids. If the all-groups resource has view-members or manage-members, the filter is a nonexistent group and both search and count return nobody the admin should see. If it does not, the set stays empty: search skips the DB filter and then applies canView in memory (so the new tests pass on a tiny user set) while getUsersCount() is still called with an empty group set and returns 0, and paginated search drops members who are not in the first page of all users. The type resource named "Groups" is also included by findByType and must not be treated as a group id.

findings.title: Per-group resources are created without a type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource() creates the authorization resource for a group (name = group id) and sets scopes, but never calls setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). init() does set the type on the all-groups resource. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers candidates only via resourceStore.findByType(..., "Groups"), so individual group resources created for group permissions are invisible to that query. User search/count then cannot be restricted to the groups whose members the admin may view, even after the resource-id vs group-id mix-up is fixed. The same omission also leaves displayName unset, so permission listings have nothing to show for these resources.

findings.title: Group deletion and V1 permission APIs throw under FGAP V2
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), isPermissionsEnabled(), and the other GroupPermissionManagement methods unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 feature is enabled, and MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returns this class. AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on every GroupRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, and that publish is not caught, so deleting any group in any realm fails with 500 and rolls back while V2 is on. The same throw breaks the V1 GET/PUT group management/permissions endpoints, which still call these methods after requiring only the V1 feature. There is also no V2 cleanup of the authorization resource named with the group id, so those resources are left orphaned even if the exception is later swallowed.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with Groups
findings.body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, and this change adds no migration to sync the schema. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before Groups existed keep a client that has Users/Clients but not the Groups resource or the new scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members). Creating a group permission then fails because the scope does not exist. Evaluating permissions calls getResourceTypeResource(), gets null, and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() passes that null to policyStore.findByResource() (implementations call resource.getId()) and, if that returned, to resource.getScopes() — a 500 on group view/list/manage checks instead of a deny. Fresh test realms hide this because init() creates the full schema only when the client is absent.

findings.title: A per-group resource hides all-groups grants
findings.body: hasPermission() evaluates the all-groups resource only when findByName() returns null. As soon as any permission has created a resource named with that group id, later checks for that group evaluate only that resource's policies and never the all-groups resource. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all groups therefore gets 403 on a group that also has a narrower permission (for example VIEW or view-members), because the all-groups policy is not consulted. The comment in this method shows all-groups permissions are supposed to be checked explicitly; the specific-resource branch skips that. GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest never combines an all-groups permission with a per-group permission, so it does not catch the deny.

findings.title: Group resources are not resolved to a display name
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users type (username, or "All users"). Group resources created by this PR use the group id as the resource name and do not set a display name, so the fallback resource.getDisplayName() is null. Permission and policy listings for the new Groups resource type therefore show a blank name instead of the group name or path, including the all-groups resource unless its display name was set elsewhere.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. That is the contract of requireManageMembership, copied onto the next method. requireManageMembers actually throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers following the javadoc will enforce group membership changes instead of member management.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission contract does not match the method
findings.body: The javadoc says the method returns a Stream of groups with view permission. The signature returns Set<String>, and both the V1 and V2 implementations collect groups that grant view-members or manage-members, not the group VIEW scope. UsersResource uses that set as the UserModel.GROUPS membership filter. An implementor following the javadoc would return the wrong ids and either hide members the admin may see or prefilter user search by groups whose members they cannot view.
